title: Each-way bets explained: what a place pays, and when it still loses

scenes.say: An each-way bet is two bets in one. Here's what each half pays, and when a place still loses you money.
scenes.caption: An each-way bet is two bets in one. Here's what each half pays, and when a place still loses you money.

visual.title: What a place pays, and when it still loses

scenes.say: Five pounds each way costs ten pounds: five on your horse to win, and five on it to finish in the places.
scenes.caption: £5 each way costs £10: £5 on your horse to win, and £5 on it to finish in the places.

scenes.say: Say it's ten to one, and the race pays a fifth of the odds for the first three. The place part is priced at two to one. If your horse wins, both bets pay: seventy pounds back. If it finishes second or third, only the place bet pays: fifteen pounds back from your ten. Anywhere else, you lose the ten.
scenes.caption: Say it's 10/1, and the race pays a fifth of the odds for the first three. The place part is priced at 2/1. If your horse wins, both bets pay: £70 back. If it finishes 2nd or 3rd, only the place bet pays: £15 back from your £10. Anywhere else, you lose the £10.

scenes.say: The places depend on the race. With five to seven runners, it's usually a quarter of the odds for the first two. Eight or more, a fifth for the first three. Big handicaps pay three or four places. Your bet slip shows the terms that count.
scenes.caption: The places depend on the race. With 5 to 7 runners, it's usually a quarter of the odds for the first two. 8 or more, a fifth for the first three. Big handicaps pay 3 or 4 places. Your bet slip shows the terms that count.

scenes.say: Now the catch. At short prices, a place can still cost you. At three to one with a fifth of the odds, the place part pays just three-fifths: eight pounds back from your ten. A place only makes a profit when the odds are bigger than five to one, or four to one with quarter terms.
scenes.caption: Now the catch. At short prices, a place can still cost you. At 3/1 with a fifth of the odds, the place part pays just 3/5: £8 back from your £10. A place only makes a profit when the odds are bigger than 5/1, or 4/1 with quarter terms.

lines.text: Profit on a place only above 5/1 (⅕ terms) or 4/1 (¼ terms)

scenes.say: And if horses are withdrawn, the terms follow the runners that actually start: an eight-runner race cut to seven pays two places, not three.
scenes.caption: And if horses are withdrawn, the terms follow the runners that actually start: an 8-runner race cut to 7 pays 2 places, not 3.
